top_story.headline: Navy extends Washington-area custodial contract a third time after two protests
top_story.dek: The Naval District Washington bridge is one of several sole-source extensions posted October 9 that lean on stalled competitions.
paragraphs: The Navy posted a justification for a third sole-source bridge of custodial services for Naval District Washington facilities, covering October 2026 through September 2027, with NJS Joint Venture, LLC as the vendor and the value redacted. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Washington office says a Government Accountability Office pre-award protest filed March 16, 2026 delayed proposal evaluations, and a second protest filed May 22, 2026 followed the dismissal of the first.

The same day, the Army Corps of Engineers posted a bridge for Air Force fuel-facility maintenance, citing active Court of Federal Claims litigation, and the Navy posted a second one-year bridge for a legacy construction-management system run by Bahfed Corp, valued at $3,800,000.

sections.headline: Navy extends Washington-area custodial contract a third time after two Government Accountability Office protests
paragraphs: 20 new sole-source justifications and 159 new solicitations were posted October 9–10; 3 justifications and 140 solicitations already covered in earlier editions are not repeated. Four of the five must-read items are bridge contracts that keep an incumbent in place while a competition is stalled.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Navy gives a third bridge to its Washington-area custodial contractor after two protests stalled the replacement contract
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
Department of the Navy, Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Washington
blocks.text: The Navy is extending custodial services for Naval District Washington facilities for October 2026 through September 2027. The justification says a Government Accountability Office pre-award protest filed March 16, 2026 delayed proposal evaluations, and a second protest filed May 22, 2026 followed the dismissal of the first; with no time left for a new award and a 30-day transition, it picked the incumbent. This is the third bridge for the contract.

blocks.title: Army Corps of Engineers bridges fuel-facility maintenance for the Air Force while a bid protest is in court
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
Department of the Army, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Huntsville Engineering and Support Center
blocks.text: The Army Corps of Engineers is awarding a sole-source bridge of up to 336 days for preventive and corrective maintenance and emergency repair of the Air Force fuels program in the North Atlantic Division, for the Defense Logistics Agency. The justification says Court of Federal Claims litigation is active and the follow-on contractor cannot begin performance, and that without a bridge the government would have no contractor after September 28, 2026.

blocks.title: Navy buys a second one-year bridge for a legacy construction-management system, citing the shutdown
meta: limited-source order (only one company can do it)
Department of the Navy, Naval Facilities Engineering Systems and Expeditionary Warfare Center
blocks.text: The justification authorizes a 12-month bridge extension of a task order for maintenance and database-migration support of the legacy eCMS system used for Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command construction management. The Navy blames a 43-day partial federal government shutdown at the start of fiscal year 2026 and the wait for a Defense Information Systems Agency provisional authorization for stalling the transition, and says Bahfed is the incumbent and exclusive authorized reseller of the legacy platform.

blocks.title: Navy keeps CACI on a budget-defense system because only the incumbent can reach its data
meta: only one company can do it
Department of the Navy, Naval Supply Systems Command Fleet Logistics Center San Diego
blocks.text: The Navy is giving CACI a follow-on contract for technical and analytical support of the Aviation Cost Evaluation System, which supports Naval Air Forces budget defense. The justification says only CACI can reach the legacy data on commercial servers needed for a migration to a government cloud. Separately, this pipeline logged an October 8 justification for CACI at the General Services Administration, a task order ceiling increase valued at $152,779,419.

blocks.title: Air Force picks brand-name SpaceX Starshield terminals for aeromedical evacuation communications kits
meta: Department of the Air Force, 763rd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron
blocks.text: Air Mobility Command wants eight TUCK-19 routing and automation kits and four SpaceX Starshield terminals to build tactical communications kits for aeromedical evacuation. The justification says no other platform has reached the same level of low-size, low-weight hardware and software automation integration, and describes the pairing as a new requirement.
Also worth a look

sections.headline: General Services Administration awards a $21.3 million Nuclear Regulatory Commission office renovation
paragraphs: Nine new awards of $2 million or more were reported, none tied to the White House or the Executive Office of the President. A further 94 new awards under $2 million were screened.

blocks.text: Largest new awards

Matos-Grunley Joint Venture won $21,292,000 from the General Services Administration (Public Buildings Service) on October 8 to renovate the second and third floors of One White Flint North in Rockville, Maryland, for the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. It is the largest new award in the window. Award.

NAPC & HSCC JV LLC received $10,720,445 from the Department of Veterans Affairs on October 8 to renovate ground-floor halls and walls at a hospital; the award record does not name the facility. Award.

Birmingham Industrial Construction, LLC won $8,400,000 from the National Aeronautics and Space Administration on October 8 for phase 3 of revitalizing pressure and propellant systems, classified as utility repair and alteration. Award.

Signature Science LLC received $3,283,470 from the Federal Emergency Management Agency on September 30; the description says the action exercises option period four of an environmental consulting task order and replaces an earlier contract number. Award.
Other new awards of $2 million or more

Fasone Construction, Inc. — $2,235,736 across two General Services Administration task orders for federal courthouse hardening, at the Richard H. Chambers Courthouse in Pasadena, California, and the Ronald Reagan Federal Building in Santa Ana, California (Pasadena $1,147,810, Santa Ana $1,087,926).

Four awards worth $1,851,526 in total cite Executive Order 14398 in their descriptions.

sections.headline: Education Department's $25.6M held pending OMB information request; Justice apportions $896.6M under continuing resolution rescission
paragraphs: Five new apportionment approvals were published in the past five days. Two files triggered flags for further review, and three routine non-flagged apportionments were also approved across Department of Homeland Security and independent agencies.

blocks.text: Flagged Apportionments

The Department of Education held $25,633,000 of discretionary funds pending reapportionment, citing an OMB request for additional information. The fund line, labeled "Unallocated," is available for obligation only after reapportionment to a "Category B" account. The apportionment footnote states: "Amounts apportioned on this line are available for obligation upon reapportionment to an applicable Category B line. [Rationale: OMB requests additional information on programmatic spending for some or all of the apportioned funds]." A related entry on the same apportionment document, "Total budgetary resources available," holds an additional $26,133,000 under the same rationale. Apportionment.

The Department of Justice apportioned $896,610,000 under a continuing resolution for FY2027 that authorizes operations based on FY2026 enacted levels, adjusted for rescissions and mandated transfers. The footnote cites Public Law 119-103, which provides the continuing resolution authority: "Pursuant to P.L.119-103, the Continuing Resolution rate of operations is based on the FY 2026 enacted appropriations, less rescission and adding or subtracting mandated transfers." Apportionment.
Routine Apportionments

items: Department of Homeland Security
Federal Emergency Management Agency — Operations and Support, $48,980,001 (FY2027). Apportionment.
United States Coast Guard — Operations and Support, $535,617,686 (FY2027). Apportionment.
Other Independent Agencies
U.S. Agency for Global Media — International Broadcasting Operations, $126,863,900 (FY2027). Apportionment.
